SMTO-LLM-0002 — The selected model can't use SMTO's tools

GUID: 44bae3b8-785e-4ea9-866a-517f0e494ab4
Slug: native-tools-unsupported
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • To take actions, SMTO needs the model to reply in a special tool format. This model connection doesn't support that, so SMTO stopped instead of guessing from plain text.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card and select Check saved model to see which check fails. The result shows whether the model server rejects tool requests, which confirms this is the problem.
  2. Ask the person who runs the model server to turn on tool calling for this model, or to recommend a model that supports it. Many model servers support tools only when a setting for the model's tool format is turned on.
  3. If a model with tool support is available, enter it on the Main card (or use Discover models), select Save Main, and start a new task. A model that supports tools lets SMTO carry out actions safely.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and a new task runs its steps without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server. Don't turn off SMTO's safety checks to get around this; SMTO never runs commands it only finds in plain text.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model client or endpoint cannot provide the native structured tool-call channel required for this Agent decision (no native tool method, or the provider rejected the tools request).

What this means

  • Agent decisions need a structured tool name and arguments that SMTO can validate before execution. This category covers a client without native tool support and a provider response classified as rejecting tools. The provider wording is a clue, not proof that software is missing.

Why this can happen

  • The selected client may not implement native tool calls, or the endpoint may reject the tools request. The adapter branch or provider status distinguishes these cases.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether the failure came from the local client interface or from an HTTP rejection. For a provider rejection, have its operator check the serving template and tool parser.

How to fix it

  • Point the role at an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint that accepts tools and tool-result messages, and enable the serving model's tool template/parser (for vLLM, --enable-auto-tool-choice with a matching --tool-call-parser). The provider's wording is a clue, not proof; verify with Check saved model, and note SMTO never executes tool-like prose from text-only endpoints.
  • Use an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint with modern tools and tool results. Configure the serving model's tool template/parser. Text-only endpoints may support Conversation mode; smTO never executes tool-like prose.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected client and endpoint return one complete, valid native tool response in a controlled test.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Covers both an absent native client method and a provider rejection classified by bounded tool-related markers.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
